description:
FOUND s494h (Opus, 2026-09-28) while probing #2006(b); PRE-EXISTING on main 209e7533.

An embedded `my` inside the RHS (or any operand) of ANOTHER `my` declaration statement is not a
lexical at all: it becomes the PACKAGE cell of that name.  The embedded-my site in
Pl/Parser2.pm `_lower_block` (`_embedded_my_names`, the `open my $fh` / `weaken(my $p = ...)`
arm) only handles a plain PPI::Statement / Statement::Expression; a Statement::Variable
(`my $ok = open(my $o, ...)`) takes the declaration path, which binds `$ok` and leaves `$o`
unbound -- it reads and writes the forward-declared global cell.

Reproducer (scratch/s494h/probe/declrhs.pl):
  sub f { my $ok = open(my $o, "<", $0); return \$o }
  my $x = f(); my $y = f();
  print $x == $y ? "same cell\n" : "fresh cell\n";          # perl: fresh cell   PCL: same cell
  my $n = 0; { my $t = ($n = 1) + (my $inner = 5); }
  print defined($main::inner) ? "leaked: $main::inner\n" : "scoped\n";   # perl: scoped  PCL: leaked: 5

Consequences: recursion / closures share one cell; the #2006(b) handle licence cannot apply
(no `let` to wrap), so `my $ok = open(my $o, ">", $f); ...` in a block keeps its handle open
until exit -- a silent late flush, and `$main::o` is visible.

Fix direction: the declaration path should bind the embedded names of its RHS in the SAME
let it builds for the declared names (fresh containers, registered with _reg_lex) -- the
chained-declarator arm (`my @a = my @b = ...`) already collects nested `my` names; the general
case is any `my` token nested in the RHS at statement level (not inside a block/anon sub).
Probe the break case: `my $x = my $x = 1` (perl: masks, one variable).
subject: An embedded `my` inside ANOTHER `my` declaration (`my $ok = open(my $o, ...)`, `my $t = ... (my $inner = 5)`) is the PACKAGE cell, not a lexical -- shared across calls, visible as $main::o (pre-existing)
